name: Hauser's Twisting Type N Wave
description: The one vacuum gravitational wave of Petrov type N whose rays twist that is known in closed form. Isidore Hauser found it in 1974; its single free function solves a linear equation of second order, and its rays spread and twist about one another everywhere off the singular sets where the field ends.
convention: Every coordinate is a pure number and the length $L$ carries the dimensions, so no factor of $c$ appears. The Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.
history: Far from a source that radiates, its gravitational field is approximately of Petrov type N, the type of a pure wave [bicakpravda1998]. The Weyl tensor of such a field has one principal null direction, repeated four times, and the light rays along it form a congruence whose expansion and twist measure how neighbouring rays spread and rotate about one another [godazgar2021]. Every vacuum of type N whose rays do not twist is known, the plane-fronted waves and the waves of Kundt and of Robinson and Trautman among them [bicakpravda1998]. Isidore Hauser, at the Physics Department of the Illinois Institute of Technology in Chicago, sent Physical Review Letters a twisting one on 26 August 1974 [hauser1974]. His abstract is one sentence: "I have found a type-$N$ gravitational field for which the principal null direction has nonzero twist and which admits exactly one Killing vector" [hauser1974].¶The letter appeared on 28 October 1974, and a correction followed on 16 December, because its equation (15) carried a typographical error [hauser1974erratum]. The field rests on a single function $f(y)$ of one variable, which obeys $16(1 + y^2)f'' + 3f = 0$ [novoseller1975, hauser1974erratum]. Daniel E. Novoseller solved that equation exactly in 1975, in Gauss hypergeometric functions [novoseller1975]. The solution even in $y$ is $f = {}_2F_1(-\tfrac18, -\tfrac38; \tfrac12; -y^2)$, and an odd one joins it to give the general solution [ivanov1999]. Hauser published the full derivation in 1978, together with explicit forms of the solution and the coordinate ranges in every case, and called it a family of twisting type N fields with one parameter [hauser1978].¶In the coordinates of the twisting algebraically special vacua, $r$ is an affine distance along each ray, $u$ labels the rays' wave surfaces and the complex $\zeta$ runs across them, and two functions $P$ and $L$ of $u$, $\zeta$, and $\bar\zeta$ fix the whole metric [godazgar2021]. Hauser's field has $L = 2i(\zeta + \bar\zeta)$ and $P = (\zeta + \bar\zeta)^{3/2} f(t)$ with $t = u/(\zeta + \bar\zeta)^2$, and $f$ obeys the same equation in $t$ [godazgar2021]. The twist of the rays is then $2P^2/(r^2 + 4P^4)$, which vanishes only where $f$ does. The curvature is a single complex amplitude $\Psi_4$ carried along the rays, which falls as $1/r$ far out along each one [godazgar2021].¶The field has more symmetry than its one Killing vector. W. D. Halford studied in 1979 the vacua of type N whose rays spread or twist and that admit a homothety, a flow that scales the metric by a constant factor [halford1979]. C. D. Collinson found Hauser's metric in 1980 in the canonical form Halford had obtained, with a group of homothetic motions of two parameters [collinson1980]. C. B. G. McIntosh reviewed the symmetries of the type N vacua in 1985 and named Hauser's metric the only known exact twisting solution with a group of two parameters made of a homothety and an isometry [mcintosh1985]. That group reduces Einstein's equations to ordinary differential equations, and in their reduction Hauser's field sits at the value $5/2$ of the homothetic parameter [finley1997, chinea2000]. F. J. Chinea and F. Navarro-Lérida rederived it there in 2000, and their reduction ends on Hauser's equation for $f$ [chinea2000].¶P. Sommers and M. Walker recovered flat spacetime as a limit of Hauser's family in 1976, and found that the field is not asymptotically flat, so it "cannot therefore be regarded as describing gravitational radiation from an isolated system" [sommers1976]. It is singular on some hypersurfaces as well [chudecki2018]. Every scalar built from the Riemann tensor alone or its first derivatives vanishes, as it does in every vacuum of type N, and the first that does not is built from second derivatives, $9(2\rho)^4(2\bar\rho)^4\Psi_4^2\bar\Psi_4^2$, with $\rho$ the complex rate at which the rays spread and twist [bicakpravda1998].¶Hauser's field is the only twisting vacuum of type N without a cosmological constant written in closed form, through hypergeometric functions [nurowski2008, zhang2012, godazgar2021]. J. Leroy found a twisting one with a cosmological constant in 1970, which turns flat as the constant goes to zero [zhang2012]. Paweł Nurowski found more in 2008, whose underlying CR structure differs from that of Hauser's field, so none of them reduces to it as the constant goes to zero [nurowski2008]. The few other twisting vacua of type N without a cosmological constant are known only through a nonlinear ordinary differential equation of third order [nurowski2008]. In 2021 Hadi Godazgar, Mahdi Godazgar, Ricardo Monteiro, David Peinador Veiga and C. N. Pope built from Hauser's field a Maxwell field and a scalar on the same curved background, the Weyl double copy of a twisting wave [godazgar2021].

related.text: The vacua whose rays spread without twisting. Among the type N vacua whose rays spread and twist, Hauser's is the one member written in closed form [bicakpravda1998, godazgar2021].
The type N vacua whose rays neither spread nor twist [bicakpravda1998, godazgar2021].

parameters.description: Length that sets the scale of the wave ($L > 0$); the homothety makes every value of it the same spacetime up to a change of coordinates

Hauser's function, a dimensionless function of $t$; the spacetime is a vacuum exactly where $16\left(1 + t^2\right)f'' + 3f = 0$, whose solution even in $t$ is ${}_2F_1\left(-\tfrac18, -\tfrac38; \tfrac12; -t^2\right)$ and odd one $t\,{}_2F_1\left(\tfrac18, \tfrac38; \tfrac32; -t^2\right)$, and the drawings take the even one

The coefficient of the square of the retarded one-form, $K/2 - r\,\partial_u\ln P$ in the form of the twisting algebraically special vacua with $K$ the curvature function of the wave surfaces, written with Hauser's equation used once

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, r, x, y)$, with $r$ an affine parameter along the twisting rays, $\zeta = x + iy$ the complex coordinate across them, and $t = u/(4x^2)$ the retarded coordinate $u$ of the twisting algebraically special vacua divided by $4x^2$, so that Hauser's function depends on $t$ alone. The translation $\partial_y$ is the one Killing vector, and $x\partial_x + y\partial_y + 3r\partial_r$ is a homothety that multiplies the metric by 5. A dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.
